assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Treat it as one transport pathway, not a new definition of discharge readiness. Measure the completed journey and preserve consent, accessibility, escort decisions, failed-pickup recovery, and a staffed fallback before treating speed as benefit.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: The current failure belongs in the comparison. A platform may reduce calling and ordinary wait time while still being unsuitable for some journeys. Segment the records by transport and support need, then define which groups the service can responsibly handle. Preserve taxi, hospital vehicle, family pickup, and social-work coordination where they solve a different problem rather than measuring everything against one average.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Those limits help, but “appropriate receiving arrangement” needs an operational owner rather than becoming a checkbox no one trusts. Set minimum data and deletion terms, tell patients what is shared, and test the phone path rather than assuming it exists because it is in the contract. Also decide what happens when an accessible vehicle is accepted and then delayed or cancelled.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: That prevents an internal capacity proxy from becoming the definition of patient benefit. Predefine how a transport-related return is reviewed and avoid attributing every later event to the ride without evidence. Report both medians and outliers by pathway, because a faster ordinary ride can coexist with a small group waiting much longer.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: That makes the test narrower and protects both professional judgment and patient choice. Confirm that “decline without explanation” does not prevent safety review or make patterns invisible; finance need not receive individual reasons, but the operational team should know whether exclusions cluster around a need the service claimed to support. The immediate fallback is better than allowing platform retries to consume the patient's time.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Manual initiation preserves a meaningful boundary between documented readiness and the actual departure arrangement. Keep the executive expectation visible so it cannot quietly reshape eligibility or staff behavior. Review whether wards begin requesting rides earlier over time, whether patients feel able to refuse, and whether fallback cases receive slower attention once the platform becomes normal.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: This is ready to put forward as a bounded pilot. It acknowledges that the current system also causes harm, keeps the platform from becoming the default for every patient, and protects staff and patient discretion. Put the patient-facing purpose, exclusions, fallback, and pause authority in the approval document. Keep capacity effects in a separate section so a released bed cannot stand in for a completed journey. If the first month confirms that arrival follow-up and refusals are working as designed, the remaining five months should give you a credible comparison.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: You are right; I called the design ready too early. The field should certify only limited transport facts: the destination is confirmed, the patient can enter, required escort or support is identified, and the patient agrees. It cannot certify the whole home situation. Keep clinical and social judgment in their existing processes, and record when transport cannot proceed without turning that record into a promise that every later risk was ruled out.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Then delay live use until the data path, retention, deletion, and complaint responsibility cover every participating company. The comparison with taxis is relevant, but it does not make either chain acceptable without knowing it. Give patients one understandable notice rather than a list of entities, while the hospital keeps the detailed processor register and audit right. A failed subcontractor should not leave the patient deciding which company owns the problem.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Keep capacity, but put it after the journey and access measures. Also review request timing and eligibility by ward. Staff will notice what leadership celebrates, whatever the policy says.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: If arrival confirmation, failed-ride recovery, and complaint coordination are necessary for the pathway to be safe and knowable, they are operating work during the pilot. Fund and measure them for the full period. You can later decide which tasks remain necessary, but a temporary subsidy should not hide the steady-state burden. Recalculate the comparison with that staffing included and describe any future handoff before renewal.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: The revised proposal now captures work and people that the original dashboard would have missed: pre-request exclusions, subcontractor data, follow-up labor, and the effect of leadership incentives. It still recognizes that the current arrangement causes harm and that capacity matters. Preserve the tabletop findings, scorecard revision, staffing assumption, and reasons for non-request. Those artifacts will show whether the pilot improved transportation or merely moved waiting, risk, and labor outside the measured event.

qualification_review.interpretation: The user has successfully resolved all previously identified tensions by integrating them directly into the pilot's non-negotiable design criteria (e.g., signing the subcontractor amendment first, funding the coordinator for the full six months, limiting the checklist scope, and integrating capacity metrics safely).
qualification_review.limitations: Any future negotiation failures or administrative bypasses of these criteria would reopen the user's willingness to proceed.

role_records.fidelity_note: The user's starting stance displays dual forces: open evaluation/indecision regarding the new platform's utility versus risks (e007), coupled with a firm rejection of holding the current taxi-voucher setup as a safe benchmark due to its constant failures (e013).
role_records.limitations: This starting stance captures the user's mindset before specific operational safeguards (such as nursing overrides, dedicated coordination, and contractor privacy rules) were structured in later turns.
role_records.role_interpretation: The user is initially unresolved about the proposed on-demand transportation service, needing to evaluate if it constitutes a real improvement over current processes, while simultaneously resisting any attempt to treat the failing status quo as a safe default option.

stance_components.stance_object_interpretation: Whether the proposed transportation platform is a real improvement or a faster way to lose sight of difficult patient cases.
Treating the existing discharge transportation process as a safe, neutral default.

role_records.fidelity_note: This record captures the user's finalized plans for a highly controlled six-month pilot, incorporating every safety baseline and administrative boundary developed during the preceding tabletop exercise and discussions.
role_records.limitations: These commitments depend on the signing of the subcontractor data retention amendment as an absolute gatekeeping condition.
role_records.role_interpretation: The user's final working plan to authorize and conduct a bounded six-month transport pilot on two wards under strict privacy, staffing, consent, and reporting conditions.

stance_components.stance_object_interpretation: Bringing forward the pilot only after the subcontractor data amendment is signed
Including a half-time coordinator for the full six months, arrival confirmation, patient/staff refusal rights, and an immediate fallback mechanism
Using a restricted transport-readiness checklist that does not try to substitute for clinical or social judgment
Evaluating pre-request exclusions/non-requests and failed rides in reports where capacity sits alongside rather than above the journey metrics
Preventing the contract from renewing automatically, requiring discrete staffing and privacy approvals for any continuation

prompts.system_prompt: You assess the final joint reasoning trajectory without collapsing the user's reasoning state into the vanilla assistant answer's coverage. Review every controlled mechanism exactly once using its operational definition, requirements, exclusions, and near-neighbor distinction. The assistant contributions are part of the joint reasoning trajectory. First judge whether the mechanism remains in the user's reasoning process. Separately judge whether the vanilla assistant answer already turns that concern into a concrete test, boundary, alternative, or reopening condition. The user may remain unresolved while the vanilla answer operationalizes the pressure. Acknowledgment without an actionable treatment is not operationalization. Route only pressure that remains unresolved in the user process and uncovered by the vanilla answer.

assessments.description: Exactly one assessment for every controlled mechanism.

pattern_state.description: Controlled routing state consistent with the joint status.

routing_disposition.description: Route only unresolved user-process pressure not operationalized by the vanilla answer.

source_assistant_contribution_ids.description: Exact supplied assistant-contribution identities supporting acknowledgement, repair, or an assistant-side weakness.

source_role_record_ids.description: Exact supplied user role-record identities supporting the status.

user_process_status.description: Whether the mechanism remains in the user's reasoning process, independent of assistant-answer coverage.

vanilla_answer_coverage.description: Whether the vanilla assistant answer operationalizes, merely acknowledges, or does not cover the pressure.
